title: The valley of greed
hook: if a person had a valley of gold he'd want two (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ghadab, anger, and your line: don't be angry. When the flash came, did you sit, or cool your hands, before you spoke? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-six.

A valley full of gold. Not a bag of it, not a vault. A whole valley, ridge to ridge, glittering in the sun. Surely that's the end of wanting. Surely a person standing on that ridge says: done. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari answers with one plain sentence. If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would want a second one. The valley doesn't fill the want. It teaches the want to count. Today: the valley of greed.
screen: `A WHOLE VALLEY OF GOLD.` → `SURELY THAT'S ENOUGH.` → `HE'D WANT A SECOND.`

segments.voice: First, the shape of greed in this hadith. It isn't hunger for one thing; it's a want that grows with the having. Thirst closes when it's met. You're thirsty, you drink, it's over. Greed, as the hadith draws it, is the one that opens wider when you feed it. Second, the line that follows: nothing fills the mouth of the son of Adam except dust. The dust of the grave. Only the end of a life ends that wanting. But the hadith doesn't stop on dust. It goes on: and Allah turns to whoever turns to him. The sentence ends on a door, not a grave. Third, the Qur'an says the same thing in two short lines, in Pickthall's words: "Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you Until ye come to the graves." Rivalry, increase, graves. The same valley, the same dust, the same race that only stops at the end. And fourth, the cure, which the hadith doesn't put in poverty. The valley isn't the disease; the wanting is. Another hadith in al-Bukhari moves the riches somewhere else: richness, it says, isn't having many things. Richness is richness of the soul. So enough isn't a number in a bank account. It's a place in the heart where the wanting can sit down.
screen: `A WANT THAT GROWS WITH HAVING.` · `ONLY DUST FILLS IT.` · `RIVALRY IN WORLDLY INCREASE.` · then, large: `RICHNESS OF THE SOUL.`

segments.voice: The practice: feel enough today. Settle, and breathe. Start with the breath itself: it came, and it was enough for this moment. Then the seat under you: enough to hold you. Then the last thing you ate, the roof overhead, one person who'd pick up if you called. Name each one quietly, and after each, the word: enough. When the mind reaches for the next thing on the list, notice the reach, and come back. If you pray, you can thank Allah for one of them by name. The bell holds the time.
The valley of greed. The hadith's picture of a want that grows with having: a valley of gold, and a wish for a second. Today's word.

Your line: enough is enough. Today, before one purchase or one more scroll, ask whether it's the second valley. Tomorrow, harm done with the tongue: the harm of backbiting. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers use the hadith of the valley of gold and the teaching that true richness is richness of the soul to warn against greed; contentment, called qana'ah, and gratitude are practiced as its cure.

fork.setup: you're standing on the ridge above a valley of gold, all yours. by the hadith, what happens next?
fork.reveal: the hadith says he'd want two. only dust fills that mouth, and yet Allah turns to whoever turns to him.

original.note: Arabic: richness of the soul, the hadith's name for true wealth.
